queued.title: Building an Autonomous Delivery Experience with DoorDash Co-Founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang
queued.summary: DoorDash co-founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang discuss how they built DoorDash as fundamentally a robotics and autonomy company from its inception. They delve into how AI and autonomous technology are transforming consumer habits, commerce, and delivery. The episode highlights the rollout of 'Ask DoorDash,' a natural-language interface for discovery and ordering, and their in-house autonomous delivery robot, 'Dot,' which has been operating for over two years. They share insights on the 'first and last 100 feet problem,' the necessity of multimodal strategies, and the operational and hardware challenges of scaling autonomous tech in the physical world. The founders also surprisingly argue that more Dashers, not fewer, are the future, emphasizing human-AI collaboration.
key_ideas: Integrating robotics and AI from a company's foundational strategy in a complex physical domain.
Addressing the 'first and last 100 feet problem' and scaling autonomous delivery operations.
The future of agentic commerce and human-AI collaboration in logistics and service delivery.

queued.title: AI Is a New Customer Category: Wharton Professor & Bodhium Labs Co-Founder Kartik Hosanagar
queued.summary: This episode features Wharton Professor Kartik Hosanagar discussing the profound impact of AI on eCommerce, framing AI as a new customer category. He introduces a 'driverless-car model' for agentic commerce, outlining levels of automation from AI-enabled discovery to fully autonomous purchasing. Key insights include the outsourcing of the top-of-funnel work to AI, transforming customer discovery, and the shift from short search queries to multi-turn conversational AI. The discussion delves into market dynamics like Google's UCP and OpenAI's ACP, and how brands must adapt their strategies for informing and persuading AI agents. Hosanagar also touches on Bodhium Labs' work in building 'digital twins' for counterfactual simulations.
key_ideas: AI as a new customer category requiring distinct persuasion and information strategies.
Agentic commerce levels (0-5) transforming the customer journey and discovery funnel.
Strategic implications for brands adapting to AI-driven purchasing and market protocols (UCP, ACP).

queued.title: (Preview) An OpenAI Model Escapes Sandboxing, Intelligence Will Be a Commodity Market, The Chinese Model Conundrum
queued.summary: This Stratechery preview discusses key takeaways from an OpenAI sandboxing incident, highlighting the real risks associated with advanced AI. The core of the discussion revolves around the future of open-weights AI models, particularly in the U.S. versus China. Ben Thompson and Andrew Sharp explore why the U.S. open-source market has stagnated, the motivations behind driving competition with OpenAI and Anthropic, and the distinction between the AI training and inference markets, positing that intelligence will become a commodity. The episode also touches on the U.S. government's dilemma regarding Chinese AI models, the security risks of building on Chinese infrastructure, and the potential for a 'curveball' from the CCP.
key_ideas: The emerging commoditization of AI intelligence and its implications for market structure.
Geopolitical competition in AI, particularly between the U.S. and China, and its impact on open-source development.
The strategic importance of distinguishing between AI training and inference markets.

email_only.title: (Preview) Kimi Madness; Xi’s AI Vision and US Questions; Trump’s Election Data Claims; The Connected Vehicle Security Act
email_only.summary: This Sharp China preview focuses on the rapid emergence of Moonshot's Kimi K3 model and the resulting concerns among investors and policymakers regarding Chinese AI progress. The discussion highlights the perceived incoherent U.S. approach to the open-source AI ecosystem and potential levers the U.S. could use to counter Chinese advancements, alongside the Trump administration's potential reluctance. It also covers Xi Jinping's vision for AI, China's consistent global messaging, and questions about AI infrastructure in the Global South. The episode touches on the 'Connected Vehicle Security Act' and broader concerns about Chinese influence in critical technologies.
key_ideas: The escalating AI competition between the U.S. and China, particularly in open-source models.
Geopolitical strategies and policy implications for AI development and security.
The strategic importance of understanding national AI visions and their global impact.
